title_original: Disney to grow content spend in fiscal 2027 to $26bn
excerpt_original: Company reports strong fiscal Q4; $3bn in cuts by 2029.

blocks.text: Disney reported strong fiscal fourth quarter earnings to beat Wall Street estimates and plans to increase content spend in fiscal 2027. The company has also forecast heavy cost-cutting over the next three annual cycles.
Overall revenues grew 16% year-on-year to $25.9bn and adjusted diluted earnings per share climbed 59% to $1.77. Operating income grew by 43% to $4.9bn.

CEO Josh D’Amaro expects to spend approximately $26bn in 2027, up 9% from 2026, and the outlay includes sports rights and international programming. The CEO, who succeeded Bob Iger in the role last March, said there will be $3bn in savings across Disney’s divisions by fiscal year 2029. The next round of layoffs is expected in early 2027.

Entertainment saw the highest revenue increase of any segment for the period ended October 3, climbing by 17% to $11.9bn (operating income grew by 92% to $1.3bn), while sports grew by 16% to $4.6bn, and experiences gained 15% to $10.1bn.

Streaming revenues increased year-on-year by 22% to $5.1bn and operating income more than doubled to $824m. D’Amaro said starting next quarter, the company will stop reporting operating income for Disney+ and Hulu. “We have made strong progress scaling our SVOD businesses and, as a result, see a long runway for growth and margin expansion at Disney Entertainment,” the CEO said. “We no longer believe the supplemental disclosure of SVOD operating income reflects this segment focus and strategy.”

Summer hit Toy Story 5 drew 20m views on Disney+ in its first five days on the platform. August delivered the highest month ever for viewing Marvel films and series, driven by the theatrical release of Spider-Man: Brand New Day and the debut of the Avengers: Doomsday trailer. That film opens on December 18. Disney executives said subscribers spent more than 2.6bn hours watching Marvel films and series in fiscal year 2026.

Q4 included an additional week of operations and executives estimate the 53rd week contributed approximately 17 cents to full year adjusted earnings. Next month, Disney+ will showcase the first wave of creator content through the agreement with TikTok. Shares in Disney were down 1.5% to $116.94 after trading.
